content.title: About
content.content: Bruschetta is a classic Italian appetizer consisting of toasted bread rubbed with garlic and brushed with olive oil, topped with fresh tomatoes, basil, mozzarella or other ingredients. It is popular as a light snack or a starter paired with wine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bruschetta is believed to have originated in Tuscany during the Middle Ages as a way to use stale bread.
The name comes from the Italian verb “bruscare,” meaning “to toast.”
The traditional “pomodoro” bruschetta recipe includes only tomatoes, basil, olive oil and salt.
Different Italian regions use a variety of toppings: mushrooms, prosciutto, artichokes, olives and even seafood.
Bruschetta is often served in restaurants as an “aperitivo” – a light bite before the main meal.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Fresh tomatoes and basil provide lycopene, vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Extra‑virgin olive oil is high in monounsaturated fats, which can help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread and tomatoes add fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Basil and tomatoes supply vitamin K, vitamin A and potassium.

items.title: Low in calories when portioned wisely
items.content: Bruschetta can be a light snack if made with modest amounts of oil and whole‑grain bread.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to wheat, olive oil, tomatoes or basil.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding salty ingredients such as prosciutto or olives can raise the dish’s sodium level.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improperly washed tomatoes or stale bread can harbor bacteria.

items.title: Acidity of tomatoes
items.content: People with acid reflux or gastritis may experience discomfort from the acidic tomatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toast slices of bread until golden, rub with garlic, drizzle with olive oil and top with a mixture of diced tomatoes, basil, salt and pepper. Optional additions include mozzarella, prosciutto or avocado.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bread in a dry, sealed container. Prepared toppings (tomato‑basil mix) should be refrigerated and used within 24 hours. Store olive oil in a cool, dark place.
